value: A CONTROL only licenses your other measurements if the control itself measures what its name says. tools/diachronic.py used the textbook definition of the Esperanto accusative — any -n after a vowel that can carry one — and it is 25% function words on this corpus: the single commonest 'accusative' it found was the preposition 'en' at 16% of all matches, then kun, nun, jen, tamen, sen, plus names like Aslaksen. The control read -0.35 (p=0.03), a significant trend in a quantity the Fundamento fixes, and ANALYSIS/diachronic.md consequently told readers to treat any rho below 0.35 as noise. Counting only real accusatives (-on/-ojn/-an/-ajn, the accusative pronouns, the -un correlatives, nothing in -en) gives -0.07 (p=0.66). The floor never existed. It survived two rounds of analysis because it had a plausible name and a plausible regex, and it was found only by building an accusative test carefully for an unrelated question.

A frequency counted over a PERIODICAL mixes its prose with its editorial furniture, and the furniture is written once and reprinted. Penseo 1990-2021 came out nearly even on the -ujo/-io question, 196 against 241, which would have made it the only modern source still using the old form freely. It is not: 96% of its -ujo occurrences stand inside parentheses against 44% of its -io, because Penseo is a poetry magazine that credits every contributor with their country — 'Mikaelo Bronsxtejn (Rusujo)', ia-Penseo_2012_n253_nov:31. That is one editor's byline template repeated across a hundred issues, not a hundred writers' usage; in Penseo's running prose the split is 8 -ujo to 136 -io, where every other modern periodical sits. Before quoting any count over periodical material, check whether the hits are in mastheads, bylines, contributor lists or addresses. The same shape as the Lanti finding and the 26 issues of The Esperantist: a rate that looks like usage is one repeated source.

Map-reduce subagent batches share ONE scratchpad directory. In mining round 4 three of eight reviewers reported that a sibling agent overwrote their intermediate file: one analysed ~100 candidates from the wrong shard before noticing a count had changed (ĉiuspeca 19->25). Verdicts themselves were safe — each agent writes only its own shard through review_shard.py --apply — but the working files are not. When launching parallel agents, put the shard or agent id in EVERY filename you tell them to write, and say explicitly that the directory is shared.

Corpus sources, archive.org, re-evaluated 2026-09 (supersedes the 2026-08 note): MIXED, and the search itself has a trap. THE LANGUAGE CODE: query language:(esperanto) OR language:(epo) — NOT esperanto alone. The items actually tag themselves epo. Searching language:(esperanto) AND year:[1940 TO 1990] returns 22 items, almost all mislabelled herpetology catalogues and Japanese botany, and would lead you to conclude the period is empty. Adding OR language:(epo) returns 966. That error nearly closed a bead as unreachable.

WHAT IS THERE 1940-1990 (966 items): 1940s=84 1950s=158 1960s=194 1970s=228 1980s=267. Largest series: Boletin 272, EsperantoPanorama 106, esperanto_aldono 87, FrancaEsperantisto 73, BelgaEsperantisto 54, EsperantistaVegetarano 51, EsperantistoSlovaka 32. Esperanto-UEA (the UEA journal) runs right through the war years. Many are uploaded by kontakto@bitarkivo.org, a curated Esperanto archive, and carry DjVuTXT, so text is downloadable at https://archive.org/download/ID/ID_djvu.txt

QUALITY IS PER-ITEM AND MUST BE TRIAGED, never accepted wholesale. Sample of 7 from 1950-1985: EsperantistaVegetarano_1971_n01 scored 93.7% known / 1.6% singles (excellent); EsperantoPanoramo_1972 45%; esperanto_aldono_76 35.3%/13.9%; and THREE returned only 18 tokens — the _djvu.txt exists but is empty, so check token count before scoring. Sample of 6 Sennaciulo 1927-1934: two usable (85.7%/2.9%, 88.5%/2.8%), three marginal, one empty. Roughly a third pass a strict bar (>=80% known, <5% singles).

LICENCE IS THE BLOCKER, not availability. These items carry no licenseurl and no rights field at all. Pre-1930 is plausibly PD; 1940-1990 is mostly still in copyright. RAW/PROVENANCE.md requires an honest licence basis per source, so this needs a human decision before fetching.

Dating heuristics fail in ways that manufacture findings, not just noise. tools/date_sources.py takes the EARLIEST plausible year in a text's first 40 lines; Omelka's La Alaska stafeto opens 'Mi naskigxis en la jaro 1904' and came out dated 1904 when it was written in 1951. Paired with his 1937 book that read as ONE AUTHOR moving -ujo -> -io over 33 years, which is the strongest form of diachronic evidence there is, and it was a birth year. Corrected it runs the other way and says nothing. Exactly one file in the corpus has that shape and it was the one that mattered. Two smaller ones in the same tool: the Vikifontaro author regex used an Esperanto-alphabet whitelist so Moliere and Prevost failed on their accents and became '(unattributed)'; and 26 issues of The Esperantist were 26 anonymous files, which inflated the count of independent pre-1911 hands. When a result looks strong, go read why each date is what it is.

Diachronic analysis: the UNIT of observation decides the answer, not the statistic. Same four measures over the same 69 dated texts: compound tenses read rho=-0.35 p=0.003 with each TEXT an observation, and rho=-0.16 p=0.30 with each AUTHOR pooled into one. Nothing about the language differs between those lines — an author with six dated texts simply stopped counting as six pieces of evidence. In this corpus author and period are confounded by construction, so tools/diachronic.py --by-author is the row to read and --by-text is a trap. Also: the accusative CONTROL is not perfectly flat (-0.27, p=0.08 at author level), so any |rho| below about 0.3 here is inside what a Fundamento-fixed quantity produces. Only -ujo/-io clears it (-0.57, p=0.003, still -0.45 p=0.025 without the two authors it leans on most).

Google Groups 429 (esp-r8p): as of 2026-08-30 the block is NOT datacenter-only. Egress IP is residential (BT UK, 86.153.76.111, btcentralplus.com) and still gets 429 on every groups.google.com/g/* and /group/* page load. Scope is Groups-only: www.google.com and google.com/search return 200 from the same IP; groups root / returns 302; POST to /batchexecute reaches app layer (404 on bad RPC name, not blocked). No Retry-After header, persistent across retries and across sessions. Conclusion: IP was likely flagged by this machine's own probing; recommendation is to stop hammering from this IP and run tools/scrape_groups_probe.py from a different network, or wait days-weeks for the flag to lapse.

The 14 bd memories live only in .beads/embeddeddolt/, which is gitignored, so their durable home is refs/dolt/data — and that ref is 403-blocked from Claude-on-the-web sessions (esp-r2n), whose containers are ephemeral. So .beads/memories.jsonl is committed as a passive export alongside issues.jsonl and interactions.jsonl. Restore with 'bd import .beads/memories.jsonl'; refresh it with 'bd export --include-memories' filtered to _type=memory. This is a data export, not a MEMORY.md: 'bd remember' is still the interface. Re-export whenever you add a memory in a web session, or the memory dies with the container.

pg-62394 (de Saussure, Ascendo al Monto-Blanka) is written in René de Saussure's REFORMED Esperanto: ankore 13 / anke 8 with zero ankoraŭ / ankaŭ, plus balde, almene, apene, ambe, morga, eŝta. A round-5 reviewer proposed excluding the file. Do NOT: it scores 95.0% recognisable over 9467 tokens, so exclusion would lose 9k tokens of ordinary Esperanto to suppress a closed set of about eight reformed grammatical words, and it is the only file in the corpus containing any of them. A round-4 reviewer already settled them as lemmas glossed as archaic/reform variants, which is the right treatment.

Playwright/ms-playwright Chromium on this NixOS-WSL box failed to launch (pid 9630: libglib-2.0.so.0 missing) — FIXED 2026-08-30 by extending programs.nix-ld.libraries in /etc/nixos/configuration.nix (glib,nss,nspr,atk*,atspi,cairo,pango,cups,dbus,expat,gtk3,libdrm,libgbm,libxkbcommon,mesa,systemd,xorg.*) + nixos-rebuild switch; backup at /etc/nixos/configuration.nix.bak-nixld. RAW/ corpus mechanics: Wikisource text lives in the Paĝo: namespace (ns=104), NOT ns=0 — main-namespace pages are ProofreadPage transclusion stubs averaging 525 bytes. Wikitext templates must be resolved, not deleted: eo.wikisource wraps emphasis, dictionary entries ({{VdE}}) and language marks ({{lang|xx|text}}) in templates, so deleting them silently eats words. Join a book's pages BEFORE stripping markup, since ProofreadPage splits constructs across page breaks; but strip each page's <noinclude> first, because that pattern is unbounded.

The reviewer failure mode that keeps costing this dictionary real words: a mined -i form is rejected as an 'inflection' because an -o or -a entry for the same root already exists. It is not an inflection — povo and povi are two words from one root, neither inflecting the other. Verdicts found so far, each self-referential nonsense: povi 'regular participle of povi', fiksi 'past passive participle of fiksi', forlasi 'infinitive of forlasi, judged separately in this shard', rediri 'past tense of rediri', trakuri, diskuri, sorcxi, volvi, remburi. The symptom to look for: the dictionary holds fiksa, fikse, fikseco and fiksigxi but not fiksi; forlasebla and forlaso but not forlasi. When reviewing a mining shard, an -i candidate whose root is already present under another ending is the case to look at hardest, not to wave through.

Two kinds of claim in this project's prose need two different treatments, and conflating them is how figures rot. A LIVE figure tracks data that changes (inventory counts from DICT/entries.jsonl, corpus frequencies) and must be machine-checked: it carries an inline HTML-comment marker naming the expression behind it and tools/check_figures.py re-evaluates it, exiting non-zero on drift, with --fix to rewrite. A STUDY RESULT (a rho, a p-value, a calibration threshold) describes one analysis run and must NOT auto-update, because silently changing it rewrites a finding rather than maintaining a total; date it instead. Live figures went stale three times undetected before this existed — the dictionary's own verb count, and Francio quoted as 1 occurrence against a real 85.

Verify every number before writing it into prose, including ones you 'know' from the analysis you just ran. Writing up the transitivity field I asserted komenci as the transitive half of komenci/komencigxi — it measures 18.4% and comes out 'uncertain', because 46% of its occurrences are followed by an INFINITIVE (li komencis demandi) and the measure counts nominal objects. Then I asserted plenigi/plenigxi as an example pair; plenigi is not a dictionary entry at all. Both were caught only by grepping entries.jsonl for the exact figures after writing them. The habit that works: after drafting any passage with numbers, run a script that re-reads each claimed figure from the source file and prints OK/MISMATCH. Two wrong claims in one document, both plausible, both would have shipped.
